learn.hook: 'How tall is Riya?' has one answer. 'How tall are the students in Class 7?' needs data — that's statistics!
points: Statistics means collecting, organising, analysing, interpreting and presenting data.
A statistical question expects answers that vary, so we need data: 'How long do students take to reach school?'
A non-statistical question has one fixed answer: 'What time does our school start?'
A statistical statement is a conclusion supported by data: 'Half the class walks to school.'
A representative value, like the mean or median, is one number that sums up a whole data set.

example.q: 36 students: Walk 18, Bus 9, Cycle 7, Car 2. Write one statistical statement.
example.answer: Half of the students walk to school

learn.reallife: Before an election, a cricket series or a school fair, people collect data to answer statistical questions.

games.title: Statistical or not?
items: How tall are the students in Class 7?
How tall is Riya?
How many siblings do children in our colony have?
What is the capital of Kerala?
How long do students take to reach school?
How many legs does a spider have?

games.title: Steps of statistics
items: Collect data
Organise it in a table
Analyse it (mean, median, ...)
Interpret what it tells us
Present it in a graph or report

quiz.q: Which is a statistical question?
options: How many hours do Class 7 students spend on homework each day?
How many hours did I sleep last night?
quiz.explain: Different students give different answers, so we need to collect data.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any question with a number in the answer is statistical

quiz.q: Which question is NOT statistical?
options: How many books do families in our building own?
What time does our school start?
What are the heights of players in our team?
How much pocket money do students in our class get?
quiz.explain: The school start time has one fixed answer; no data collection is needed.
quiz.mistake: Confuses a fixed fact with varying data

quiz.q: Which order describes the work of statistics?
quiz.explain: First we gather data, then arrange it, study it, draw meaning and show it.
quiz.mistake: Starts with drawing graphs before collecting data

quiz.q: Data for 36 students: Walk 18, Bus 9, Cycle 7, Car 2. Which statement does the data support?
options: Bus is the most common way
Half of the students walk to school
quiz.explain: 18 out of 36 is exactly half.
quiz.mistake: Reads the wrong row of the table

quiz.q: How many students are there in the data Walk 18, Bus 9, Cycle 7, Car 2?
quiz.explain: Add every group: 18 + 9 + 7 + 2 = 36.
quiz.mistake: Counts the number of groups instead of students

quiz.q: What is a representative value of a data set?
options: One number that sums up the whole data set
quiz.explain: Values like the mean and the median represent the whole data set with a single number.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any single value from the list will do

quiz.q: Using Walk 18, Bus 9, Cycle 7, Car 2, which statement is NOT supported by the data?
options: More students walk than take the bus
Fewer than 10 students take the bus
quiz.explain: The data shows how students travel, not what they like — and only 7 cycle.
quiz.mistake: Accepts a claim the data says nothing about

quiz.q: Three students scored 6, 7 and 8 marks. Which is a representative value?
quiz.explain: The mean (6 + 7 + 8) ÷ 3 = 7 sums up the marks.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the total with a representative value

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'Is how many birds visit my tree each day a statistical question?' Explain!
teach.praise: Yes! The answer changes day to day, so Gappu needs data.
teach.nudge: Does the question have one fixed answer or many different answers?

learn.hook: Arjun scored 32, 45, 18, 50 and 25 runs. Is he a '34-runs player'? The mean tells us his typical score!
points: Data is a collection of facts or numbers, like the runs scored in matches.
Putting data in a table makes it easier to read and compare.
The mean (average) = sum of all the values ÷ number of values.
The range = biggest value − smallest value. It shows how spread out the data is.
If every value goes up by the same amount, the mean goes up by that amount too.

example.q: Arjun's runs in 5 matches are 32, 45, 18, 50 and 25. Find the mean and the range.

learn.reallife: Cricket batting averages, average marks in a class and the average rainfall of a month are all means.

games.title: Mean truths
items: The mean is always one of the numbers in the data.
The mean of 1 and 2 is 1.5, which is not in the data.
Mean = sum of the values ÷ number of values.
That is how the mean is found.
If every value is increased by 2, the mean also increases by 2.
The sum grows by 2 for each value, so the mean grows by 2.
The range is the biggest value minus the smallest value.
It measures the spread of the data.
The mean of 0, 0, 0 and 12 is 12.
Sum 12 ÷ 4 values = 3.
Adding a new value equal to the mean does not change the mean.
Example: 2, 4, 6 has mean 4; 2, 4, 6, 4 also has mean 4.

quiz.q: Arjun scored 32, 45, 18, 50 and 25 runs in 5 matches. What is his mean score?
quiz.explain: Sum = 170. Mean = 170 ÷ 5 = 34 runs.
quiz.mistake: Gives the total instead of dividing by the number of matches

items: M1
M2
M3
M4
M5

quiz.q: The highest temperatures in Jaipur for a week were 28, 30, 31, 27, 29, 32 and 33 degrees. What is the mean?
quiz.explain: Sum = 210. Mean = 210 ÷ 7 = 30 degrees.
quiz.mistake: Picks the middle number in the list without calculating

quiz.q: What is the range of 12, 7, 19, 3, 15?
quiz.explain: Biggest 19, smallest 3. Range = 19 − 3 = 16.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the first and last numbers in the list instead of the biggest and smallest

quiz.q: The mean of 4 numbers is 15. What is their sum?
quiz.explain: Mean = sum ÷ 4, so sum = 15 × 4 = 60.
quiz.mistake: Divides 15 by 4 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: The mean mark of 5 students is 40. A sixth student scores 52. What is the new mean?
quiz.mistake: Averages 40 and 52 directly, as if there were only two values

quiz.q: Weekly pocket money: Riya ₹50, Kabir ₹70, Meena ₹60 and Joseph ₹100. What is the mean?
quiz.mistake: Averages only the middle two values

items: Riya
Kabir
Meena
Joseph

quiz.q: For the data 5, 5, 5, 5, which is correct?
quiz.explain: Sum 20 ÷ 4 = 5, so the mean is 5. Biggest − smallest = 5 − 5 = 0.
quiz.mistake: Gives the sum as the mean, or the value as the range

quiz.q: The mean of 6, 8 and x is 8. What is x?
quiz.explain: The sum must be 3 × 8 = 24. So x = 24 − 6 − 8 = 10.
quiz.mistake: Thinks x must equal the mean

teach.ask: Gappu's friends scored 6, 8 and 10 in a game. How does he find the mean score?
teach.nudge: After adding all the scores, what do you divide by?

topics.title: Fair shares, dot plots and zeros

learn.hook: A batter scores 0 in a match — that 0 counts! But a match washed out by rain? That's missing, not zero.
points: The mean is a fair share: if 4 friends with 3, 5, 6 and 10 laddoos share equally, each gets (3 + 5 + 6 + 10) ÷ 4 = 6.
A dot plot puts a dot above a number line for each value; tall stacks show values that repeat.
From a dot plot you can quickly see the smallest, the largest, the most common value and the spread.
Zero is a real value and must be counted. Missing data (like a match not played) is left out.
The mean and median always lie between the smallest and the largest values — never outside the range.

example.q: A batter's scores are 30, 0, 45, 0 and 25. Find the mean and the median.

learn.reallife: Cricket averages count every out, even ducks (0 runs), but skip matches that were not played.

games.title: Fair and missing
items: A mean can be bigger than the largest value
It always lies between the smallest and largest values.
A score of 0 runs should be counted as a value
The batter played and scored 0.
A match that was not played should be counted as 0
It is missing data and is left out.
In a dot plot, a tall stack shows a value that appears often
Each dot is one value.
The mean is what each person gets if the total is shared equally
That is the fair-share idea.

items.q: Mean of 10 and 20 (missing value left out)

quiz.q: 4 friends have 3, 5, 6 and 10 laddoos. They share all of them equally. How many does each get?
quiz.explain: Total = 24, shared among 4: 24 ÷ 4 = 6. That is the mean.
quiz.mistake: Gives the total instead of the share

quiz.q: A dot plot shows the values 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 5, 5. Which value has the tallest stack of dots?
quiz.explain: 3 appears three times, more than any other value.
quiz.mistake: Picks the largest value instead of the most common

quiz.q: For the dot plot 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 5, 5, what is the range?
quiz.explain: Range = largest − smallest = 5 − 2 = 3.
quiz.mistake: Counts the dots instead

quiz.q: A batter scores 30, 0, 45, 0 and 25 in five matches. What is the mean score?
quiz.explain: The zeros count: 100 ÷ 5 = 20. Leaving them out would wrongly give 100 ÷ 3.
quiz.mistake: Leaves out the zero scores

quiz.q: For the scores 30, 0, 45, 0, 25, what is the median?
quiz.explain: Sorted: 0, 0, 25, 30, 45. The middle value is 25.
quiz.mistake: Takes the middle value without sorting

quiz.q: One of the matches in a series was washed out by rain. How should it be treated when finding the batter's mean?
options: Leave it out — it is missing, not a score of 0
Count it as the highest score
quiz.explain: No runs were scored because no match happened, so it is missing data.
quiz.mistake: Treats missing data as zero

quiz.q: Can the mean of 4, 8 and 9 be 10?
options: No — a mean always lies between the smallest and largest values
Yes, the mean can be any number
quiz.explain: The mean is 21 ÷ 3 = 7, between 4 and 9. It can never be above 9.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the mean can lie outside the data

quiz.q: What is the median of 3, 7, 7, 12?
quiz.explain: Even count: the median is the mean of the two middle values, (7 + 7) ÷ 2 = 7.
quiz.mistake: Gives the mean (7.25) instead

teach.ask: Gappu's team played 5 matches; one was washed out and in one Gappu scored 0. How should Gappu find the average?
teach.praise: Fair and correct! Gappu counted the 0 and left out the washed-out match.
teach.nudge: Which of the two is a real score, and which is missing data?

learn.hook: If one billionaire walks into a tea stall, the 'average' wealth there shoots up! The median stays calm. Let's see why.
points: The median is the middle value after arranging the data from smallest to largest.
If there is an even number of values, the median is the mean of the two middle values.
The mode is the value that appears most often. Data can have more than one mode.
One very big or very small value can pull the mean far away, but the median hardly changes.
Use the mode for 'most popular' questions, like the most common shoe size.

example.q: Find the median and the mode of 4, 9, 2, 7, 4, 10, 6.
steps: 7 values, so the middle one is the 4th: 6
4 appears twice, more than any other value

learn.reallife: Shoe shops stock the mode size most, and news reports often use the median income because it is not pulled by a few very rich people.

games.title: Match each list to its median
Median or mode?
items: The middle height in a line of students
The most popular shoe size to stock
The favourite ice-cream flavour
A typical salary when one person earns a huge amount
The bus route taken by most children
The middle score after lining up test marks

quiz.q: What is the median of 4, 9, 2, 7, 4, 10, 6?
quiz.explain: Arrange: 2, 4, 4, 6, 7, 9, 10. The middle (4th) value is 6.
quiz.mistake: Takes the middle of the list without arranging it first

quiz.q: Shoe sizes in a group: 5, 6, 6, 7, 6, 8, 5. What is the mode?
quiz.explain: Size 6 appears 3 times, more than any other size.
quiz.mistake: Picks the biggest value or the middle value

items: Size 5
Size 6
Size 7
Size 8

quiz.q: What is the median of 12, 15, 18, 20?
quiz.explain: There are 4 values, so the median is the mean of the two middle ones: (15 + 18) ÷ 2 = 16.5.
quiz.mistake: Picks one of the two middle values

quiz.q: Five friends have pocket money of ₹10, ₹12, ₹11, ₹13 and ₹104. What is the median?
quiz.explain: Arrange: 10, 11, 12, 13, 104. The middle value is ₹12.
quiz.mistake: Calculates the mean (₹30) instead of the median

quiz.q: For the pocket money ₹10, ₹12, ₹11, ₹13 and ₹104, why is the median a better 'typical' amount than the mean?
options: The mean cannot be calculated here
The ₹104 pulls the mean up to ₹30, but the median stays near most values
quiz.explain: Four friends have about ₹10–13. The mean (₹30) is pulled up by one large value, while the median (₹12) shows a typical amount.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the mean is always the best average

quiz.q: Riya's cricket scores are 0, 25, 25, 30, 40 and 50. What is the median?
quiz.explain: 6 values, so take the mean of the 3rd and 4th: (25 + 30) ÷ 2 = 27.5.
quiz.mistake: Gives the mode (25) or one middle value

quiz.q: Can a set of data have more than one mode?
options: Yes, for example 2, 2, 5, 5, 7 has modes 2 and 5
No, there is always exactly one mode
Only if all values are different
No, the mode must be the middle value
quiz.explain: If two values appear equally often and more than the others, both are modes.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the mode, like the median, is always a single middle value

quiz.q: What is the median of 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9?
quiz.explain: There are 9 values in order. The middle one is the 5th value, which is 5.
quiz.mistake: Divides the count by 2 and gives 4.5

teach.ask: Gappu has the numbers 7, 3, 9, 5, 1. How does he find the median?
teach.praise: Chirp! 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 — the middle one is 5. Gappu found the median!
teach.nudge: What must you do to the numbers before picking the middle one?

topics.title: Comparing groups and the story of the mean

learn.hook: About 500 years ago, 16 men lined up their left feet, toe to heel, outside a church to decide how long 'one foot' should be!
points: To compare two groups, put their dot plots side by side and compare their means and medians.
A higher mean does NOT mean every member is bigger — compare spreads too.
In 16th-century Germany, 16 men stood with their left feet toe to heel. That line was a 16-foot rod, and one-sixteenth of it was taken as one 'foot' — really the mean of the 16 feet.
Indian mathematicians had words for the mean: samīkaraṇa, 'levelling' (Mahāvīrācārya, about 850 CE) and samamiti, 'mean measure' (Bhāskarācārya, about 1150 CE). 'Sama' means equal.

example.q: Which class is taller on average: 7A (140, 142, 145, 147, 151) or 7B (138, 144, 146, 150, 152)?

learn.reallife: Doctors compare children's heights today with data from years ago to see how nutrition has changed.

items.q: 16 feet total 480 cm: the mean foot

games.title: Comparing fairly
items: To compare two classes, comparing one student from each is enough
One student does not represent a whole class.
The 'mean foot' came from lining up the feet of 16 men
The total was divided by 16.
If class B's mean height is higher, every student in B is taller
Some B students can be shorter than some A students.
Dot plots side by side help us compare spread
We can see where values bunch up.
Bhāskarācārya used the word 'samamiti' (mean measure) for the mean
'Sama' means equal: the mean is the equalising value.

quiz.q: Class 7A heights are 140, 142, 145, 147 and 151 cm. What is the mean height?
quiz.explain: Total 725 cm ÷ 5 = 145 cm.
quiz.mistake: Gives the total instead of dividing

quiz.q: Class 7B heights are 138, 144, 146, 150 and 152 cm. What is the median height?
quiz.explain: The values are already sorted; the middle (3rd) one is 146 cm.
quiz.mistake: Picks a value next to the middle

quiz.q: 7A has mean height 145 cm and 7B has mean height 146 cm. Which statement is correct?
options: 7B is taller on average, by 1 cm
Every 7B student is taller than every 7A student
The two classes are exactly the same
quiz.explain: 146 − 145 = 1 cm, so 7B is taller on average.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a higher mean means every member is bigger

quiz.q: 7B's mean height is higher than 7A's. Must every 7B student be taller than every 7A student?
options: Yes, because the mean is higher
No — 7B's shortest student (138 cm) is shorter than 7A's shortest (140 cm)
quiz.explain: A mean summarises the group; individual values can overlap.
quiz.mistake: Confuses group averages with individuals

quiz.q: 16 men's left feet lined up measure 480 cm in total. How long is the 'mean foot'?
quiz.mistake: Divides by 10 instead of 16

quiz.q: Bhāskarācārya called the mean 'samamiti' (mean measure). What does 'sama' mean?
quiz.explain: 'Sama' means equal. The mean is the equal (fair-share) value that stands for the whole collection.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the mean is the largest value or the total

quiz.q: A school claims, 'Our Class 7 students are taller than Class 7 students 20 years ago.' What data would check this?
options: The mean heights of Class 7 students now and 20 years ago
The height of the tallest student today
The number of students in Class 7
quiz.explain: We need comparable data from both times, summarised by a representative value.
quiz.mistake: Uses a single extreme value to judge a group

quiz.q: Two groups guessed one minute (in seconds). P: 50, 55, 60, 65, 70. Q: 40, 58, 60, 62, 80. Both have mean 60. Whose guesses are more spread out?
options: Group Q — its range is 40 seconds
quiz.explain: Range of P = 70 − 50 = 20; range of Q = 80 − 40 = 40. Same mean, different spread.
quiz.mistake: Thinks equal means tell us everything

teach.ask: Gappu's class has a higher mean height than the next class. Gappu says everyone in his class is taller. Is that right?
teach.praise: Correct! A mean describes the group, not every single member.
teach.nudge: Could one student in Gappu's class be shorter than someone in the other class?

learn.hook: A good graph is like a picture that talks — one look and you know which day sold the most samosas!
points: A bar graph uses bars of equal width; the height of each bar shows a value.
The scale tells what one unit stands for, like 1 unit = 10 students.
A double bar graph puts two bars side by side to compare two groups.
A line graph joins points (connects the dots) to show how something changes over time, like temperature through the day.
Always read the title, the labels and the scale before reading values.

example.q: A bar graph shows books read: Mon 4, Tue 7, Wed 3, Thu 6. Which day had the most books, and what is the total?

learn.reallife: Weather reports use line graphs for temperature, and schools use bar graphs to show results of sports day.

games.title: Which graph fits best?
items: Favourite fruits of a class
Your height every year from age 5 to 12
Number of students in each section
Temperature every hour of a day

quiz.explain: Tuesday has the tallest bar (7 books).
quiz.mistake: Picks the first or last bar instead of the tallest

Tue

quiz.explain: Add the heights of all the bars: 4 + 7 + 3 + 6 = 20.
quiz.mistake: Reads only the tallest bar

items: Mon
Tue
Wed
Thu

quiz.q: In a bar graph, 1 unit stands for 50 trees. A bar is 6 units tall. How many trees does it show?
quiz.explain: Each unit is 50 trees, so 6 units = 6 × 50 = 300 trees.
quiz.mistake: Reads the height without using the scale

quiz.q: An ice-cream stall sold 45 cones on Saturday and 60 on Sunday. How many more cones were sold on Sunday?
quiz.explain: 60 − 45 = 15 more cones on Sunday.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two days instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: A line graph shows temperature: 9 am 22°, 12 noon 30°, 3 pm 28°, 6 pm 24°. When was it hottest?
quiz.explain: The highest point of the line is at 12 noon (30°).

items: 9 am
12 noon
3 pm
6 pm

quiz.q: From the same line graph (12 noon 30°, 6 pm 24°), by how many degrees did the temperature fall from 12 noon to 6 pm?

quiz.q: A double bar graph shows Class 7A: 18 boys, 20 girls and Class 7B: 22 boys, 15 girls. How many more students does 7A have than 7B?
quiz.mistake: Compares only the boys or only the girls

items: 7A boys
7A girls
7B boys
7B girls

quiz.q: A bar graph starts its scale at 50 instead of 0. The bars for 55 and 60 make one look twice as tall as the other. What is true?
options: 60 is only a little more than 55; the graph exaggerates the gap
The graph is fine to read as it is
quiz.explain: 60 − 55 = 5, which is a small difference. Starting the scale at 50 makes the gap look huge.
quiz.mistake: Judges values by how bars look instead of reading the scale

teach.ask: Gappu sees a bar graph for the first time. How should he read it?
teach.praise: Super! Read the title and scale, then compare the bar heights. Gappu can read graphs now!
teach.nudge: What tells you how much one unit on the graph stands for?

learn.hook: A graph with 12 tiny bars is hard to read. Put the tiny ones together as 'Others' and the picture becomes clear!
points: When there are many small categories, combine them into 'Others' to keep the graph clear.
Two-step reading: first read what is given (the values), then infer (differences, most, least, trends).
To draw a double bar graph, choose a scale, draw a pair of bars for each category, and add a key (legend) showing which colour is which group.
Infographics mix pictures and numbers. Check each claim against the numbers before believing it.

example.q: Favourite sports: Cricket 14, Football 8, Kabaddi 5, Chess 2, Hockey 1, Badminton 2. Group the smallest ones as 'Others'.
steps: New table: Cricket 14, Football 8, Kabaddi 5, Others 5

learn.reallife: News channels show election results and weather data as infographics — reading them carefully stops you from being fooled.

games.title: Given or inferred?
items: Cricket got 14 votes
Cricket is the most popular sport
Football got 8 votes
Cricket got 6 more votes than football
Kabaddi got 5 votes
Girls borrowed more books than boys on two of the days

items.text: In a double bar graph, the ___ tells which colour is which group
If 1 unit = 5 books, a 3-unit bar shows ___ books

quiz.q: Chess 2, Hockey 1 and Badminton 2 are grouped as 'Others'. How many votes does 'Others' get?
quiz.mistake: Counts the number of sports instead of the votes

quiz.q: Why do we group small categories into 'Others'?
options: To keep the graph simple when some categories are very small
To make every bar the same height
quiz.explain: Many tiny bars make a graph cluttered; one 'Others' bar keeps it readable.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 'Others' is used to hide data

quiz.q: Cricket 14, Football 8, Kabaddi 5, Others 5. How many votes were cast in all?
quiz.mistake: Leaves out the 'Others' group

quiz.q: Which of these is an inference rather than a value read directly from the graph?
options: Cricket got 6 more votes than football
quiz.explain: The difference 14 − 8 = 6 is worked out from two given values.
quiz.mistake: Treats a read value as an inference

quiz.q: A double bar graph shows books borrowed (boys, girls): Mon 12, 15; Tue 10, 14; Wed 16, 11. On which day did boys borrow more than girls?
quiz.explain: Only on Wednesday is the boys' bar (16) taller than the girls' bar (11).
quiz.mistake: Compares the wrong pair of bars

quiz.q: In the same graph (girls: 15, 14, 11), how many books did girls borrow in all?
quiz.mistake: Adds the boys' values too

quiz.q: What must a double bar graph have so readers know which bar is for boys and which is for girls?
quiz.explain: The key shows which colour or pattern stands for each group.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the title alone explains the bars

quiz.q: An infographic shows Cricket 14 and Football 8 but says 'Most students like football'. Is the claim true?
options: We cannot tell from the numbers
No — cricket has more votes than football
quiz.explain: 14 > 8, so the claim does not match the numbers.
quiz.mistake: Trusts the pictures instead of the numbers

teach.ask: Gappu drew a graph with 10 bars, and 6 of them are tiny. How can Gappu make it clearer?
teach.praise: Neat graph! Gappu's 'Others' bar keeps it clear.
teach.nudge: What could Gappu do with all the tiny categories?

topics.title: Data detective: trends, combined means and a lock puzzle

learn.hook: A lock's code is hidden behind five clues. Like a data detective, rule out digits one by one!
points: Time-series tables show values year by year. Find the change each year to estimate the next value: 120, 135, 150, 165 → about 180.
Combined mean: find each group's total, add the totals, then divide by everyone: 20 students averaging 40 and 30 averaging 50 give 2,300 ÷ 50 = 46.
The median splits sorted data into two equal halves.
Estimate vs measure: the absolute difference = how far an estimate is from the actual value, ignoring the sign. Average these to judge how good estimates are.
Data projects: decide a question, collect data (survey), organise it, summarise it and present it.

example.q: Group A: 20 students, mean 40 marks. Group B: 30 students, mean 50 marks. Find the mean of all 50 students.

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers estimate next month's sales from past months' data — a time series in action.

games.title: Detective checks
items: The mean of two groups is always halfway between their means
The bigger group pulls the combined mean towards its own mean.
If an estimate is 52 s and the actual is 60 s, the absolute difference is 8 s
The median splits sorted data into two equal halves
Half the values are below it and half above.
In the clue '738: nothing is correct', 7, 3 and 8 are not in the code
So we can rule them out.
A data project starts by drawing a graph
It starts with a question to investigate.

quiz.q: A library had 120, 135, 150 and 165 visitors a day in 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024. About how many might it have in 2025 if the pattern continues?
quiz.explain: The number grows by 15 each year: 165 + 15 = 180.
quiz.mistake: Repeats the last value

quiz.q: Group A: 20 students, mean 40 marks. Group B: 30 students, mean 50 marks. What is the mean for all 50 students?
quiz.mistake: Averages the two means without using group sizes

quiz.q: Why is the combined mean in that question 46 and not 45?
options: Group B has more students, so its mean counts more
Means always go up when groups join
quiz.explain: 30 students at 50 outweigh 20 students at 40, pulling the mean above 45.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every group counts equally

quiz.q: Sorted heights (cm): 132, 135, 138, 140, 143, 145, 149, 151. What is the median?
quiz.explain: 8 values: the median is the mean of the 4th and 5th: (140 + 143) ÷ 2 = 141.5.
quiz.mistake: Gives the mean of all values instead

quiz.q: Riya estimates one minute as 52 seconds. What is the absolute difference from the actual 60 seconds?
quiz.explain: |52 − 60| = 8 seconds. The absolute difference is never negative.
quiz.mistake: Keeps a minus sign

quiz.q: Three estimates differ from the actual time by 8 s, 5 s and 2 s. What is the average difference?
quiz.mistake: Gives the total difference

quiz.q: What is the first step of a data project such as 'How long are the sentences in our textbook?'
options: Decide clearly the question to answer
quiz.explain: A clear question tells you what data to collect.
quiz.mistake: Starts with the graph before collecting data

quiz.q: Lock clues: 682 — one digit right and in place; 614 — one right, wrong place; 206 — two right, wrong places; 738 — none right; 870 — one right, wrong place. What is the code?
quiz.explain: 738 rules out 7, 3 and 8. From 870 and 206, 0 is in the code but not 2nd or 3rd, so it is 1st. From 682, 2 is right and in place (3rd). From 614, 4 is in the code but not 3rd, so it is 2nd: 042.
quiz.mistake: Does not use every clue

teach.ask: Gappu's class (20 students, mean 40) joins another (30 students, mean 50). Gappu says the new mean is 45. Help!
teach.praise: Detective Gappu cracked it: the combined mean is 46!
teach.nudge: What are the total marks of each group?
